Q: "UserStyleSetting has a 640 x 464 icon. This is too big" error when building Wear OS Watch Face A:

I've managed to solve this, and the issue is in the way the drawable folder is handled. As mentioned in this answer, the icons will get scaled up if necessary, so the solution is to put all the drawable elements into a drawable-nodpi folder (or another folder with the relevant qualifier) so they won't get upscaled.

Though in my case I just shrunk my icons down to 128px on the longest side. On my Pixel Watch 3 they're only a centimetre or two wide so it doesn't affect me too much.

Q: Is exit syscall invoked implicitly? A:

Here's another angle on things: What happens if you write a program in pure assembly language, without making any use of the C library, and you don't invoke the _exit system call when you're done? For example, save this as demo.s (this demo will work on either x86-64 or -32 with an ELF assembler):

    .text
    .global _start
    .type _start, @function
_start:
    ret

and then compile and run it, and you get ...

$ cc -static -nostdlib -nostartfiles test.s
$ ./a.out ; echo $?
Segmentation fault
139

... an abnormal termination! At the machine language level, a program can only "terminate correctly" by invoking the _exit system call.

(If you run this program under an assembly-language debugger, set a breakpoint on _start, and inspect the CPU state when control reaches the breakpoint, what you'll discover is that the kernel didn't bother making a fake stack frame as-if _start had been called. It just cleared most of the registers, set the stack pointer to point to the "bottom" (highest address) of the space usable for the call stack, set the program counter to the address of _start, and then allowed the new process to begin execution. Thus ret has nowhere to return to, and the program crashes.)

(Exercise for you: Somewhere on your computer's disk is a file named crt1.o. Find it. Disassemble it. Compare the disassembly to my little demo. What does it do?)

Q: Populating a listbox with a range based on a combobox selection on a userform A:

The process followed by me is summarised below. UserForm Initialise Routine set relation between ComboBox and ListBox and Worksheet reference. Though I have genralised for a more general situation of Contact address list which could be of use to many persons.

Private Sub UserForm_Initialize()
    Set rData = ActiveSheet.Range("A1").CurrentRegion
    Me.ComboBox1.List = rData.Offset(1).Value
    Me.ListBox1.ColumnCount = 6
    Me.ListBox1.List = Me.ComboBox1.List
End Sub

ComboBox Change Routine has following code.

Private Sub ComboBox1_Change()
  Me.ListBox1.ListIndex = Me.ComboBox1.ListIndex
End Sub

There is a close Button to close the form.

Private Sub cmdClose_Click() Unload Me End Sub

General declarations as Follows.

Option Explicit
Dim rData As Range
